title: 2 dead in Bering Sea as teen survivor found clinging to side of capsized boat
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A 15-year-old boy survived for days in the frigid Bering Sea, clinging to an overturned boat and desperately trying to hold onto his older brother and another crew member before both men drowned.

The teenager, identified by family as Derek Parker, was found alive Monday afternoon on the capsized 18-foot skiff about four miles east of Alaska’s St. Lawrence Island, according to the US Coast Guard.

His older brother, who was captaining the boat, and a second crew member were recovered dead from the water.

The boy’s mother told Alaska News Source that her youngest son had survived for days without food or water after the boat overturned. His older brother became trapped beneath the vessel, she said, while the third crew member survived alongside Derek for another day before dying.

Family members said the teenager tried to hold onto both men, even after they drowned.

“He held onto the other two as long as he can even after they drowned. He is alive,” his aunt wrote in a heartbreaking Facebook post.

The three had departed the Siberian Yupik village of Savoonga Friday and were expected to return by 3 a.m. Sunday, according to the Anchorage Daily News.

Alaska State Troopers alerted the Coast Guard that the group was overdue around 8:30 p.m. Sunday.

Poor weather and limited visibility prevented a Coast Guard aircraft from reaching the search area until Monday morning, while troopers and local authorities searched from shore.

At about 3 p.m., an HC-130 Hercules aircrew spotted the overturned boat and the teenager clinging to it.

The crew dropped a life raft and survival equipment, then coordinated with the nearby fishing vessel Northwest Explorer to reach him.

“Before departing the scene to refuel, the HC-130 aircrew deployed a line of flares to guide the Northwest Explorer to the overturned vessel,” the Coast Guard said.

The fishing vessel rescued Derek, who was suffering symptoms of hypothermia, and recovered the two unresponsive men from the water. All three were taken to Nome, Alaska.

The older brother, whose name was not provided, leaves behind two children, according to Alaska’s News Source.

A family GoFundMe described the tragedy as a devastating loss for the small community.

“My nephew and one of his crew members passed away doing what he loved, out in the Bering Sea. My other nephew was found alive. Our village is mourning the loss of two,” the fundraiser states.

The family is seeking donations to help with travel and to bring the deceased men home. The aunt said the funds would also support her sister and the surviving teenager.

“Our hearts go out to the families, friends, and communities affected by the tragic loss of these two mariners,” Rear Admiral Bob Little, commander of the Coast Guard’s Arctic District, said in a statement.

“We are grateful for the incredible efforts of the motor vessel Northwest Explorer, Federal, State, Village first responders and mission partners who assisted in the effort that resulted in a life saved.”

Savoonga, a village of about 800 people, sits on the northern coast of St. Lawrence Island, more than 160 miles west of Nome and roughly 40 miles from Russia.
